question: What does reproductive health mean beyond simply being free from disease?

options.A: The total eradication of maternal mortality in rural communities
options.B: Ensuring every woman gives birth to at least four children
options.C: Having access to free maternity drugs in public health facilities
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health encompasses holistic well-being across physical, mental, and social dimensions, not just the physical absence of illness. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h1)

question: How does the modern definition of reproductive health influence the daily work of a midwife?

options.A: It restricts her responsibilities strictly to managing normal deliveries
options.B: It shifts her primary duty to treating newborn infections only
options.C: It requires her to focus exclusively on family planning commodities
options.D: It guides care to cover overall well-being and personal reproductive choices

explanation: Because reproductive health involves safe sex, reproductive capability, and personal choice, midwives must look beyond the physical body to support overall wellness and autonomy. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h1)

question: What major shift in global health policy occurred at the 1994 Cairo Conference?

options.A: Mandating a specific number of children per family across developing nations
options.B: Banning traditional birth attendants from assisting rural deliveries
options.C: Moving from demographic population control to individual reproductive rights
options.D: Establishing the first global guidelines for managing postpartum haemorrhage

explanation: The Cairo Conference famously shifted the global focus away from strict population number targets and onto human rights and individual empowerment. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why was the shift introduced at the Cairo Conference especially important for women?

options.A: It recognised their autonomy, health, and rights as central to development
options.B: It transferred all leadership roles in hospitals strictly to female staff
options.C: It guaranteed them free tertiary education in all developing countries
options.D: It eliminated the need for antenatal checkups during normal pregnancies

explanation: By placing women's rights and health at the centre of the agenda, the conference ensured that healthcare systems would support personal choice rather than force demographic targets. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which group is included in the broad scope of reproductive health services besides women of childbearing age?

options.B: Only newborn babies under one month old

explanation: Reproductive health spans the entire life cycle and involves all members of the community, including men, adolescents, and older individuals. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h3)

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach activity. Which action fits best within the scope of reproductive health services?

options.A: Treating chronic hypertension and stroke in elderly patients
options.B: Administering mass vaccination against polio for infants
options.C: Providing counselling on family planning and screening for sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Conducting routine dental checks for primary school children

explanation: Family planning and infection screening are core components of reproductive health services. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is required for reproductive health services to be properly delivered at the primary health care level?

options.A: Mandatory hospitalization for every pregnant woman
options.B: Exclusively private funding from international donors
options.C: Strictly high-tech surgical theaters in every village clinic
options.D: Availability, accessibility, acceptability, and good quality

explanation: Health service delivery standards require that care be accessible, available, acceptable to the local culture, and maintained at a high standard of quality. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why are functioning referral pathways essential for reproductive health care delivery?

options.A: They allow primary clinics to transfer all routine antenatal work away
options.B: They prevent midwives from ever performing normal vaginal deliveries
options.C: They eliminate the need for community health education programmes
options.D: They ensure women with severe complications reach higher-level facilities quickly

explanation: Quick and efficient referral systems save lives when unexpected obstetric emergencies arise that primary clinics cannot manage. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h4)

question: How can a Nigerian midwife best respect reproductive rights in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: By forcing every client to accept the same family planning method
options.B: By ensuring informed consent, patient confidentiality, and bodily autonomy
options.C: By ignoring local cultural beliefs completely during consultations
options.D: By restricting health education strictly to married women over thirty

explanation: Respecting reproductive rights requires upholding the client's right to make private, informed choices about their own body and health. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge a midwife might face when applying the Cairo framework in Nigeria?

options.A: Navigating complex cultural and religious values regarding family planning
options.B: Addressing high rates of teenage pregnancy and unsafe abortion
options.C: An immediate excess of fully equipped tertiary hospitals in every rural ward
options.D: Overcoming structural and economic barriers in primary health care

explanation: Rural areas in Nigeria typically face a shortage, not an excess, of well-equipped health facilities, making this statement incorrect. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T1#BMP310_U1_T1_h5)
